{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOUDROfM8AAAABeiNDVw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlR_zzhIDOUk", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlR_z", "number": 306, "title": "Simplify toolbar graph menu: Graphs → Open, remember last opened, and name-order fallback", "body": "## Goal

Simplify the Chrome extension **toolbar icon right-click context menu**, remove the redundant manual left-click default chooser, and make the most recently **explicitly selected graph from the Open menu** the graph used by subsequent toolbar **left-clicks**.

When there is no valid previously selected graph (first run, deletion, corruption/non-runnable entry), choose the **first runnable graph in ascending name order** automatically. No separate "Choose a default" workflow is needed.

This replaces the older deliberate separation between right-click launch and default selection in #267. It also completes the user-facing "Live" naming cleanup begun in #277.

## Desired native context menu

```text
Graphs ▶
  Open ▶
    ✓ Meeting Assistant
      Translation
      Transcription
  Graph Library
```

- The outer menu is **Graphs**, not **Live graphs**.
- Put the saved runnable graph names under a single **Open** submenu (rather than many direct "Open <name>" entries under Graphs).
- Display the **last-selected/current left-click graph with the native checked state** in that Open list. Prefer `chrome.contextMenus` `type: 'radio'` so exactly one entry is checked, using browser/OS-native UI. Do not inject Unicode checkmarks into item labels.
- Put **Graph Library directly under Graphs**, as a sibling of Open, not under Open.
- **Remove the entire "Default for left-click" submenu** and its duplicated graph list.
- Selecting any graph under **Open** must (a) persist it as the latest selected graph for left-click and (b) open **a new independent execution window** for that graph, using the *actual invoking tab*. Merely hovering must not update selection.
- Subsequent **left-click** on the extension toolbar icon opens the last selected graph in a new execution window (and does not start recording automatically). Repeated left-clicks need not change that selection.
- Preserve Chrome's native `contexts: ['action']` integration and built-in extension management entries; do not add custom launcher UI.

## Selection and fallback rules

Treat the current stable graph ID stored as `library.assignments.live` as the persisted **last-selected graph ID**, reusing existing migration/locking and avoiding a new storage schema or user-facing "default" control.

1. **Valid previous selection:** If the saved ID still identifies a runnable top-level graph, use it for left-click and mark its Open menu entry as checked. Preserve this across browser/extension worker restarts.
2. **No stored selection / initial install:** Enumerate runnable top-level graphs, sort by ascending display name and automatically pick **the first**. Persist the chosen ID for consistent left-click and menu check state.
3. **Previously selected graph deleted / invalid / no longer executable:** On the next library refresh/launch, automatically pick the **first remaining runnable graph in name order**, persist it and show that graph checked. Do not require the user to open the menu and choose manually.
4. **No runnable graphs:** Do not invent a selection or launch a different invalid graph. Show an appropriate disabled/empty Open item and retain an actionable path to **Graph Library**. Left-click should surface a clear actionable error or path to create/repair a runnable graph, preserving existing error visibility.
5. **Name and tie-breaking:** Use consistent locale-aware name sorting, e.g. `Intl.Collator('ja', { numeric: true })` and stable ID tie-breaker, for Latin alphabet and Japanese kana. Kanji reading order is not inferred. Use the **same ordering for the Open list and fallback selection**, ideally aligned with #297's Graph Library name-order semantics. Renames may reorder choices; they should **not change a still-valid selected ID**. Only fallback when the ID becomes unusable.
6. **Eligibility:** Only include actual runnable top-level saved graphs (no invalid drafts, missing dependency graphs, or non-runnable reusable subgraph definitions), retaining the current `usable(entry, library)`/graph validation rules. Avoid treating "first graph in storage" or newest-edited as name-first.

## Correctness and lifecycle

- Use the existing offscreen-host `launchLibrary()` path in [`extension/launch-library.js`](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/extension/launch-library.js) and the serialized `GraphLibrary.change()`/Web Lock persistence mechanism; avoid races between toolbar menu refresh, fallback re-selection, renames, deletes, and concurrent invocations.
- A right-click **Open** choice should **commit the last-selected ID and validate it** before launching (no wrong-graph fallback if the chosen entry vanished or save failed). If selection commit/validation fails, show an actionable error; do not pretend another graph was selected.
- Maintain **one window/session per intentional launch** and its own graph ID; changing the last-selected ID must never retarget an already-open window or modify an active runtime graph snapshot.
- Preserve original tab context and user gesture/activeTab permission behavior on right-click selections. Left-click also retains its invoking tab.
- Refresh the native menus on library edits (create/rename/delete/graph validity changes), extension install/startup, and service-worker recreation. Ensure checked item and fallback match persisted selection after refresh; avoid menu creation races.
- Existing identifiers such as `assignments.live`, internal operation names and file names may remain for compatibility; **user-facing menu text** should not say "Live graphs", "Live default", or "Default for left-click". Update user-facing error guidance accordingly.

## Code touchpoints

- [`extension/background.js`](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/extension/background.js):
  - Current root ID `live-graphs` has title `Live graphs`; current `live-run:<id>` entries are immediate children titled `Open <name>`.
  - There is a separate `live-defaults` submenu and `live-default:<id>` radio entries; remove that structure and its default-only click handler.
  - Introduce an **Open** submenu under root; place radio graph items there; on click update selection and launch; keep Graph Library directly beneath root. Update left-click error text.
  - Internal IDs can remain stable or be adjusted as necessary; no stale menu handlers.
- [`extension/launch-library.js`](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/extension/launch-library.js):
  - Currently `live-list` returns `defaultId`, `live-default` explicitly changes `assignments.live`, and fallback only selects the sole runnable graph.
  - Adapt to **automatic first-name fallback whenever no valid selection exists**, including when several runnable graphs exist; implement a safe atomic selection update and an explicit user-picked graph selection operation usable from Open.
  - Avoid write/notification loops: do not persist if the current valid selection is unchanged.
- [`extension/graph-library.js`](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/extension/graph-library.js): retain stable IDs, revision checks, storage migration and graph eligibility. Only modify if needed for a safe shared helper; no format change.
- [`tests/extension/toolbar-launch.spec.js`](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/tests/extension/toolbar-launch.spec.js): update old manual-default tests and menu hierarchy assertions; add cases below.
- [`docs/extension-graph.md`](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/docs/extension-graph.md) and relevant toolbar validation docs/help: update UI instructions so they no longer describe `Live graphs → Default for left-click`.

## Acceptance criteria / tests

- [ ] Right-click hierarchy is exactly **Graphs → Open → (checked runnable graph list)** with **Graph Library** next to Open under Graphs. No `Live graphs` label, repeated `Open <name>` item text at list level, or Default for left-click submenu.
- [ ] Opening graph B via Open creates its own execution window **and** updates the persisted last-selected ID; a subsequent toolbar left-click opens B; B is checked in the Open list.
- [ ] First install with multiple runnable graphs and no valid stored selection automatically checks/opens the first by alphabetic/Japanese kana name order. Same for a deleted/invalid last-selected graph.
- [ ] Valid selection remains stable across names being edited, sort reordering, worker restart and extension restart. Persisted fallback is deterministic; ties are stable.
- [ ] Open menu list is name-ordered and excludes broken/unrunnable graphs and standalone subgraph definitions.
- [ ] Empty/no-runnable library retains usable Graph Library navigation and clear left-click error, not a wrong launch.
- [ ] Two or more different graph windows remain independent, and menu/left-click launches preserve the proper invoking browser tab and no automatic Start.
- [ ] Concurrent selection/menu refresh cannot accidentally select or launch an unintended graph, and no redundant persistent writes happen on ordinary reads.
- [ ] Existing toolbar and graph library tests pass; update any tests that asserted separate default selection or no selection with multiple graphs. Report automated coverage and manual native-menu limitations honestly.

## Coordination / out of scope

- [#277](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/issues/277): already removed misleading Live from the execution window; this issue fixes remaining toolbar-facing naming.
- [#267](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/issues/267): the prior choice to keep Open and default selection separate is deliberately **superseded** for the toolbar menu.
- [#297](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/issues/297): Graph Library name-order sort; align comparator behavior where feasible.
- Do not redesign Graph Library itself, the in-page Web microphone's *separate* right-click graph chooser, or the execution window. Do not change underlying graph runtime or introduce cross-window reuse.
